changes_vs_current: New topic. SCOPE: smartphone apps of any category. Google's own apps (Google search app, Gmail, Google Maps, Chrome) are in because every reach and download source has them high (Similarweb 2023 MAU #3/#4/#12/#16; Apple 2025 downloads #3/#9/#8/#18). Apple's stock apps (Messages/iMessage, Camera, Safari, Photos, Weather) are out: none of the usage or download sources measure them, and the only data I saw (YouGov apps/websites ratings: iMessage 81% fame, 58% popularity) comes from a list that leaves out most major apps, so it can't be compared. Google Photos and Google Drive also left out (background utilities; Drive has only 1 source). RAW AVERAGE ORDER (6 people sources, missing = list length + 5): 1 YouTube, 2 Instagram, 3 Facebook, 4 TikTok, 5 WhatsApp, 6 Google, 7 Gmail, 8 Amazon, 9 Snapchat, 10 Google Chrome, 11 Google Maps, 12 Reddit, 13 ChatGPT, 14 X, 15 Messenger, 16 Pinterest, 17 Spotify, 18 Walmart, 19 Google Photos, 20 Discord, 21 Netflix, 22 Cash App, 23 Telegram, 24 Roblox, 25 Temu, 26 Threads, then Google Drive, Shein, Venmo, CapCut, LinkedIn; Uber was outside the top 40. GUT-CHECK MOVES: Facebook 3->2 (ahead of Instagram in Pew, Morning Consult and Android DAU; the raw gap was 0.4). Amazon 8->5 (#2 MAU in 2023 and #4 Android DAU 2025; its raw score is dragged down only by the social-only Pew and Morning Consult lists). Netflix 21->10: in every all-category source it sits around Spotify/Reddit (MAU #22, Android DAU #18, pageviews #10), and the social-only lists penalize it for being out of scope; it is the top US streaming service and a gut top-6 answer. Spotify 17->13 for the same social-list reason (Apple #17, Android DAU #10). Uber in at 18: a gut answer that the data really does put lower (MAU #40 in 2023, missing from the 2025 Android DAU top 50), so it moved only into the tail, not into the top 12. Google search app 6->11 and Chrome 10->21: high reach because they are preinstalled defaults, but people listing 'apps on my phone' name them less readily. X stays at 14 and Snapchat at 7; WhatsApp 5->6. Google Photos (raw 19) and Telegram (raw 23) were dropped to make room for Uber and Netflix: Photos is a background utility, and Telegram's US numbers are niche next to Temu (in 3 sources, raw 25, very well known in the US). Roblox kept at 24 on its 3 sources.
confidence: High for 1-4 (YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok are top in every source). Medium-high for 5-12 (Amazon, WhatsApp, Snapchat, Gmail, Google Maps, Netflix, Google, ChatGPT): all have 3+ sources, but their order depends on how much weight goes to reach versus downloads. WhatsApp may be too high for 'what Americans name', and Netflix's spot leans on the gut check. Medium-low for 13-24: the order is loose, and Uber, Chrome and Roblox are judgment calls. Near misses: Telegram, Threads, Google Photos, Venmo, CapCut, LinkedIn, Shein, Hulu, Prime Video, Disney+, DoorDash, Waze, Apple Music. Could not read: YouGov Ratings social/apps rankings (table did not load; the apps-websites list loaded but leaves out major apps), Statista/Comscore app reach (403), Sensor Tower overall US MAU (paywalled). Rejected the Udonis/AppMagic 'US' list because it includes clearly non-US apps (QQ, Weibo, PhonePe, Meesho) and its numbers look implausible. A 2019 'apps we can't live without' poll (Facebook 21%, Instagram 11%, Gmail 8%, YouTube 8%) was not counted: it is old and the pollster isn't named. The best broad MAU source is from 2023.
